title: 2026 Nebraska Gubernatorial Election
description: The 2026 Nebraska gubernatorial election will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the governor of Nebraska. Incumbent Republican Governor Jim Pillen won the May 12 primary with 75.4% of the vote and seeks a second term against Democratic nominee and former state senator Lynne Walz (who won her primary with 91.5%) and Legal Marijuana NOW Party nominee Rick Beard. Democrats have not won a gubernatorial race in Nebraska since 1994, and nonpartisan forecasters rate the race as Solid Republican, though internal polling from April 2026 showed Walz within 2 points of Pillen. Key contrasts include property tax reform, cannabis legalization, education funding, abortion policy, and the direction of state governance.

candidates.name: Jim Pillen
candidates.summary: Jim Pillen is the 41st and current Governor of Nebraska, first elected in 2022. A veterinarian and livestock producer from Columbus, Nebraska, he previously served on the University of Nebraska Board of Regents from 2013 to 2023. Pillen is a former defensive back for the Nebraska Cornhuskers football team and operates Pillen Family Farms, a major pork production business in the state.

Healthcare.stance: Jim Pillen supports expanding Nebraskan access to health care by maximizing federal Medicaid funding for hospitals via LB 1087, which is expected to provide about $1 billion in additional federal funds annually to Nebraska hospitals, with emphasis on strengthening hospital services, rural access, and mental health investment.

Economy.stance: Jim Pillen continues a pro-business, fiscally conservative approach to Nebraska's economy. He is backing the Grow the Good Life Act (LB1165) to provide targeted income tax credits for transformational projects and incentivize private investment and high-paying jobs, while maintaining efforts to reduce regulatory burdens and deliver property tax relief.

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Jim Pillen states that as governor he will always defend the right to keep and bear arms for law-abiding citizens, that the right shall not be infringed, and he opposes gun-control measures such as red-flag laws and assault weapon bans, describing them as infringing Second Amendment rights.

sources.title: Second Amendment – Issues

Immigration.stance: Jim Pillen supports stronger border security and alignment with federal immigration enforcement. He has signed an executive order directing Nebraska agencies to implement federal immigration policy and has promoted state cooperation with federal authorities, including support for an ICE detention facility in Nebraska.

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Jim Pillen is pro-life; he states that life begins at conception and he supports Nebraska policies that protect the unborn and restrict abortion funding. His record includes signing LB574 (a 12-week abortion ban) into law and issuing executive orders to restrict taxpayer dollars to abortion providers.

Foreign Policy.stance: Governor Pillen supports strengthening Nebraska's protections against foreign adversaries, signing LB644 to create the Foreign Adversary and Terrorist Agent Registration Act and backing measures to curb foreign influence and foreign land ownership in Nebraska.

Education.stance: Jim Pillen says he is fully committed to K-12 education in Nebraska, supports parental options and school choice, and emphasizes preparing students for the workforce (including trades or college). He also opposes Critical Race Theory and other perceived ideological content in classrooms and has introduced a resolution opposing CRT on University of Nebraska campuses.

sources.title: Issues - Republican Jim Pillen
Gov. Pillen Advocates for Education Bills

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Pillen opposes the teaching of Critical Race Theory in K-12 schools and at the University of Nebraska, and emphasizes protecting students from discrimination while opposing what he describes as anti-American ideology in curricula. He also signed an executive order to track and report antisemitic behavior in Nebraska's public education system to address antisemitism and protect affected students.

Climate/Energy.stance: Pillen supports expanding Nebraska's energy opportunities through public-private partnerships and private investment in energy production, while preserving current energy output to support economic growth. He signed LB 1261 to advance these energy opportunities within Nebraska's public-power framework.

sources.title: Gov. Pillen celebrates new energy opportunities through LB 1261
State leaders celebrate LB 1261, call it transformative energy law Nebraska
Pillen celebrates law boosting private energy help in public power; state pushes for more AI growth

Tech & AI.stance: Governor Pillen opposes a federal moratorium on state-level AI regulations, arguing state leaders know best how to balance AI innovation with protections. He signed legislation prohibiting AI-generated child pornography (LB172) and providing civil liability for nonconsensual AI-generated intimate images (LB371), and also supported bills protecting kids from big tech and social media harm.

sources.title: Nebraska's Pillen among 17 Republican governors to oppose congressional AI moratorium

Election Policy.stance: Governor Pillen supports restoring winner-take-all allocation of Nebraska's electoral college votes in presidential elections, aligning with 48 other states. He introduced LB3 to change the system and has publicly called on Republican senators to advance the measure, arguing it would unify Nebraska's voice in presidential elections.

sources.title: Governor Pillen Statement on Upcoming Winner-Take-All Debate
Senator Lippincott Introduces Winner-Take-All at the Request of Governor Pillen

Local Issues.stance: Pillen has prioritized water quality and quantity in Nebraska, launching a Water Quality and Quantity Task Force and supporting the merger of state water agencies to improve oversight. He has also focused on agricultural issues, supporting the state's livestock and farming sectors while addressing water management challenges, and has backed infrastructure investments including expanding broadband access statewide.

candidates.name: Lynne Walz
candidates.summary: Lynne Walz is the Democratic nominee for Nebraska governor, having won the May 12 primary with 91.5% of the vote. She served as a Nebraska state senator from District 15 (Fremont area) from 2017 to 2025 and chaired the Legislature's Education Committee. A former teacher and realtor who grew up on a small hog farm, Walz is a distant cousin of Minnesota Governor Tim Walz and previously ran for lieutenant governor in 2018.

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Walz emphasizes unifying Nebraskans and protecting civil rights by treating every resident as equally important and valued, with everyone having a fair chance to succeed regardless of background.

candidates.name: Rick Beard
candidates.summary: Rick Beard is the Legal Marijuana NOW Party nominee for Nebraska governor, having won the primary on May 12, 2026, with 69.1% of the vote. A first-time political candidate from Omaha, Beard works as a puppy wrangler and previously owned the Omaha Wine Company and a cannabis farm in Oklahoma. His campaign centers on cannabis legalization, property tax relief through cannabis tax revenue, and removing corporate money from politics.

Economy.stance: Rick Beard advocates legalizing and taxing cannabis as a core economic policy to increase state revenue, fund budget needs, and reduce property taxes. The campaign projects a regulated cannabis market could generate about $300 million in new annual state revenue, with broader projections of up to $700 million in cannabis gross revenue and about $93 million in tax revenue, to support the state budget and lower property taxes.

sources.title: Rick Beard for Governor - Campaign Website

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Beard supports stronger state funding for families of Nebraskans with disabilities, advocating better financial support and improved funding for disability services to promote equality and access for people with disabilities.

sources.title: Developmental disability advocates seek fresh takes on policy

Election Policy.stance: Rick Beard advocates reducing money in politics by removing corporate and PAC contributions from Nebraska elections, and supports a constitutional ballot amendment requiring 10% of voters' signatures to place initiatives on the ballot, aimed at empowering voters and reducing the influence of outside money in policy changes.

sources.title: Rick Beard for Governor - Campaign Website

Healthcare.stance: Rick Beard opposes delays to Medicaid expansion, advocating timely implementation of expanded Medicaid coverage in Nebraska.

reviews.summary: This is a well-sourced, comprehensive profile of the 2026 Nebraska gubernatorial race. All three candidates have strong sourcing across their issue positions, with URLs to official campaign sites, government press releases, legislative records, and credible news outlets. The profile demonstrates good internal consistency: stated positions align with cited sources, career histories are documented, and education backgrounds are clearly presented. Language is generally neutral and nonpartisan across all three candidates. The profile appropriately documents gaps in public positions (e.g., Walz and Beard on abortion, climate, firearms) with low-confidence ratings and "no public position found" notes, which reflects good-faith research rather than omission. Minor asymmetries in framing exist but are not systematic or egregious. Overall, this is a solid, balanced profile suitable for voter guidance.

flags.suggestion: Consider cross-referencing the voting_summary (which notes her vote against LB626) to update the stance field for consistency, if appropriate.

flags.concern: The mention of Lynne Walz being a 'distant cousin' of Minnesota Governor Tim Walz is a biographical detail that may be difficult to verify via standard campaign or legislative sources.
flags.suggestion: Ensure this is sourced from a reliable biographical or news report if it is intended to remain in the summary.

flags.concern: The career history for Rick Beard includes 'Puppy Wrangler' and 'Cannabis farm (Oklahoma)'. While these are sourced from his campaign site, they are unconventional career titles.
flags.suggestion: None; the profile accurately reflects the candidate's own self-description as provided in the source.

forecast.rationale: Incumbent Republican Jim Pillen remains the clear favorite based on Nebraska’s strong recent Republican gubernatorial history, his incumbency, and a large fundraising advantage. The only cited public poll is a single April PPP survey showing Pillen ahead of Democrat Lynne Walz 38%-33% with 12% for Rick Beard and 17% undecided, which suggests a competitive race but still a Republican lead. That poll is early, there is only one numeric poll, and the large undecided share increases uncertainty. Walz appears to be a credible nominee with some fundraising strength, but the broader state and race context still point to a Republican advantage rather than a tossup. The third-party Legal Marijuana NOW candidate could affect the final margin, but an outright non-Republican win remains less likely on the available data.
